hypotheses.title: Transient Fluvial Iso-Chi Knickzone Downslope Back-Projection & Piedmont Hinge Reception (H86T-KNDS)
layers_involved: External SHA-pinned .cache/external/dem10_chi_100m_i16.tif (sha256 8897ba9c30ef1cd7ad5f23c16c6dfd7bb070e7e757f36fd9486eb45edfd973a5: Band 1 step_max_x1000, Band 2 step_min_x1000, Band 3 ksn_max_m0.9, Band 4 log10_area_m2_x1000, Band 5 zmean_m)
External SHA-pinned .cache/external/topo_10m_derived_100m_u8.tif (sha256 a6398d9950965dec6aae6ccecdaa6ced48645d133eab222cbdd11def9bdabfa4: Band 1 slope_p90, Band 7 aspect_coherence)
Native corroboration baseline: Band 2 (magnetic_rtp), Band 3 (magnetic_tmi_hg), Band 5 (dem_elevation_rel), Band 16 (mt_resistivity_2km)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Under Perron & Royden (2013) integral stream-power theory, a range-front normal fault slip pulse creates a transient channel-steepness knickzone (elevated ksn_max_m0.9 and positive chi-step step_max_x1000 - step_min_x1000) that migrates upstream into the footwall at equal chi across parallel canyons of differing drainage area A, sitting at staggered Euclidean distances L(A) ~ A^(m/n) upstream of the actual range-front fault. H86T-KNDS applies a Lahontan shoreline hypsometric notch (suppressing 1315-1355 m highstand wave-cut benches) and a symmetric-Bouguer sill veto, then projects footwall knickzone intensity downslope along the unit canyon gradient -grad(zmean_m)/||grad(zmean_m)|| across multi-scale area-weighted shifts s in {4, 8, 14, 22} px onto the piedmont basement-hinge reception zone (50 m < Z_b < 800 m, gated by horizontal gravity gradient Band 18) and filters for along-strike iso-chi coherence across adjacent canyons.
hypotheses.why_unmapped_in_catalogue: USGS QFFD and INGENIOUS aerial-photo mapping trace continuous Euclidean scarps at the range front. Where Holocene alluvial fan progradation buries the active range-front piedmont fault trace, the surface scarp disappears, while the tectonic slip signal survives 0.4-2.2 km upstream inside bedrock footwall canyons at area-staggered Euclidean positions that look non-collinear in map view.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan wave-cut shorelines (~1330 m highstand bench) and resistant Tertiary basalt/welded-tuff caprock ledges (suppressed via the 1315-1355 m Lahontan hypsometric notch filter and symmetric Bouguer gravity ridge veto).
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: H86C-KSLB, H86I-KSAD, and H86I-RLMS evaluated ksn_max_m0.9 locally at pixel (y, x), placing anomaly mass inside footwall canyons 0.5-2 km upslope of the actual range-front fault trace (outside the 300 m DTI kernel). H86T-KNDS is the first lane in GEMSDOE86 to back-project footwall chi/ksn knickzones down-canyon along -grad(zmean_m) by drainage-area-scaled distances onto the piedmont gravity-hinge reception zone, tested directly against an unprojected local-chi ablation (E2) and a zero-chi native baseline (E3).
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement_qualitative: Highest among low-cost untried geologic mechanisms: directly bridges the 0.4-2.2 km geometric offset between upstream footwall fluvial knickpoints and buried piedmont range-front faults within the 300 m DTI tolerance cone.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low (~25s CPU runtime; all required USGS 3DEP 10 m chi and native bands are local and SHA-256 verified).

hypotheses.title: Geothermal Manifestation Multi-Point Azimuthal Corridor Graph (VENT-RANSAC)
layers_involved: External SHA-pinned GDR #1391 gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv (sha256 122718e6..., dist_known_fault_px strictly excluded), gdr_volcanic_vents_in_footprint.csv (sha256 f91bafba...), paleo_geothermal_regional.zip (sha256 faffcf69...), 2m_temperature_probe_INGENIOUS_regional_data.zip (sha256 1301f70d...)

hypotheses.physical_signature: Constructs an oriented collinearity graph over thermal springs/wells (T > 35 C), 2-m temperature probe anomalies, paleo-sinter/tufa mounds, and Quaternary volcanic vents: triplets of thermal manifestations within 15 km that are collinear within +/-8 deg AND aligned within +/-12 deg of local potential-field/MT structural strike project a narrow 300 m corridor connecting the vents across unmapped step-overs.
hypotheses.why_unmapped_in_catalogue: Blind geothermal upwelling systems in sediment-filled basins (e.g., Carson Sink, Dixie Valley, Humboldt structural zone) lack surface fault scarps but leak热 fluids and deposit travertine/sinter beads along unmapped dilatational fault strands.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Topographic-low playa-margin artesian spring lines and US-highway/railroad drill-access corridors (suppressed via TIGER road-parallelism veto and iso-elevation contour veto).
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: H86I-HVFD and H86K-STDP rasterized radial Gaussian halos or up-hydraulic-head shifts around individual GDR-1391 points; no lane in GEMSDOE86 has built a multi-point azimuthal collinearity corridor graph linking triplets of thermal manifestations along geophysical strike.
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement_qualitative: Medium: high precision on blind geothermal basin step-overs, but spatially sparse outside known thermal districts.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low-Medium (~30s CPU runtime; all GDR-1391 CSV/ZIP pins are local and SHA-256 verified).

hypotheses.title: Radiometric Provenance-Step & Alluvial Fan Apex Dislocation (RCSD)
layers_involved: External SHA-pinned USGS GeoDAWN geodawn_rad_u8.tif (sha256 c22420f7...: K, eTh, eU, TC) and geodawn_extensions_u8.tif (sha256 a35a9c6d...)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Directional step-filter applied to Aitchison log-ratios ln(K/eTh) and ln(eU/eTh) specifically perpendicular to the downslope alluvial fan transport vector grad(DEM), isolating sharp cross-fan geochemical provenance steps and fault-controlled potassic/illite alteration halos while subtracting along-fan gravitational sorting trends.
hypotheses.why_unmapped_in_catalogue: Active intrabasin and piedmont strike-slip/oblique faults offset alluvial fan lobes derived from contrasting footwall lithologies (e.g., Mesozoic granodiorite vs Cenozoic rhyolite/andesite) without preserving a topographic scarp.
hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Non-tectonic depositional contact between adjacent drainage fan lobes and USGS GeoDAWN airborne survey flight-block boundaries (controlled via acquisition_block_id_100m.tif seam veto and watershed confluence boundary suppression).
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: RMRB-86, H86I-RKSC, H86P-TCWB, and H86Q-BFRA used isotropic radiometric gradients, total-count downslope wash asymmetry, or pointwise K*U/Th^2 ratios; none decomposed the radiometric log-ratio gradient into orthogonal vs parallel components relative to the downslope fan transport vector.
hypotheses.expected_dti_improvement_qualitative: Medium: targets unmapped intrabasin piedmont faults in GeoDAWN coverage, bounded by shallow regolith mixing.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low (~25s CPU runtime; GeoDAWN radiometric grids and seam masks are local and SHA-256 verified).
